**CENTRAL CONTRIBUTION:**
The study introduces CancerSB, a serious point-and-click adventure game designed for bone cancer awareness and education through culturally grounded, interactive gameplay, and presents a preliminary validation methodology using ChatGPT 4o to simulate diverse user feedback via the "mega-personas" approach for early design evaluation.

**PROBLEM AND CONTEXT:**
Bone cancer, despite accounting for less than 1% of all cancer cases, is a significant health concern, projected to result in approximately 3,970 new cases and 2,050 deaths in 2024. It predominantly affects adolescents and young adults aged 15–24, with Osteosarcoma showing a male-to-female ratio of 1.4:1, and metastatic cases reducing the five-year survival rate to 27–58%. Diagnosis delays exceeding three months increase mortality risk by 33%, highlighting the urgent need for enhanced awareness and early detection. Current health education tools lack engaging resources like serious games specifically tailored to bone cancer, primarily focusing on more prevalent cancer types.

**METHOD/SYSTEM:**
CancerSB is a serious adventure game developed in Unity, with visual assets refined using Adobe Photoshop, integrating original art, narrative, and educational content informed by medical professionals. The game employs a point-and-click adventure format within an isometric environment (Fig. 4.a-c), structuring gameplay as a journey across three culturally themed world regions: Chile, Italy, and China. Each region metaphorically symbolizes specific human bone regions affected by distinct bone cancer types: Chondrosarcoma (Chile, targeting pelvis, proximal femur/humerus, ribs, scapula, craniofacial bones, typically adults over 40), Ewing’s Sarcoma (Italy, affecting pelvis, femur, ribs, humerus, spine, common in children/adolescents), and Osteosarcoma (China, impacting distal femur, proximal tibia, and proximal humerus, more frequent in adolescents/young adults) (Fig. 3). Each country level comprises five interconnected environments centered around a hub, featuring mini-tutorials (represented by a yellow ribbon ticket) that introduce bone cancer characteristics, symptoms, and treatment strategies. Gameplay involves solving puzzles and making strategic decisions to simulate diagnostic procedures and choose among various treatment modalities (chemotherapy, surgery, radiation therapy), with progressive difficulty mirroring real-world cancer care complexity. Each region culminates in a symbolic boss battle embodying its respective cancer type: a Mayan warrior for Chondrosarcoma in Chile (Fig. 5), a minotaur for Ewing’s Sarcoma in Italy (Fig. 6), and a dragon for Osteosarcoma in China (Fig. 7). A standardized battle scene template governs these encounters, where players manage health, perform defensive or offensive actions (surgery), and utilize backpack items (treatment potions, healing, energy), noting that treatment potions cannot be used against the Chondrosarcoma boss, reflecting its resistance to conventional therapies.

For preliminary validation, the study utilized ChatGPT 4o to simulate survey responses from diverse user profiles, adapting the "mega-personas" approach [3] by Steinmacher et al. Four distinct "mega-personas" were defined: the Informed Patient (aged 35–60, with cancer experience, seeking empathetic representation, limited gaming), the Curious Student (aged 16–25, moderate-to-high gaming, valuing interactive learning), the Healthcare Professional (aged 25–65, low gaming but digitally comfortable, prioritizing clinical accuracy), and the Casual Gamer (aged 18–40, high gaming, seeking entertainment with optional education). ChatGPT 4o was prompted with persona backgrounds, descriptions of key visuals (opening scene (Fig. 2), game home (Fig. 1), battle screens), and gameplay flow diagrams to complete a seven-question Simulated Persona Feedback Questionnaire. Questions Q1 and Q2 assessed visual design appeal and appropriateness (inspired by Curve [18]); Q3 and Q4 measured navigation intuitiveness and interface simplicity (from PSSUQ [19]); Q5 evaluated gameplay flow logic and engagement (from GEQ [20]); Q6 assessed the effectiveness of educational puzzle integration (combining FSS [21] and AttrakDiff [22]); and Q7 requested five descriptive adjectives for visual aesthetics (from AttrakDiff). Responses were quantified (Likert scales 1-5 for Q1-6), aggregated, and analyzed to identify common themes and variations across personas.

**RESULTS AND METRICS:**
The simulated user feedback revealed consistently strong positive reception for CancerSB across all four "mega-personas." Visual Design (Q1) received the highest scores (rate 5) from younger personas (Casual Gamer, Curious Student), while more mature personas rated it 4. Overall visual appeal across opening, home, and battle scenes ranged from 4 to 5, although the Casual Gamer gave the lowest scores (rate 3) for general visuals/UI compared to commercial standards. Colors, Layout, and Typography (Q2) consistently scored 5 across all country scenarios and personas, highlighting excellent visual accessibility and thematic coherence, also rating 4-5 for battle scenes. Navigation (Q3) and Simplicity (Q4) consistently scored 4, indicating intuitive design with minor room for enhancements. Gameplay Flow (Q5) and Educational Puzzle Integration (Q6) were rated 4-5, with the Informed Patient and Healthcare Professional rating the educational effectiveness (Q6) highest. The Italy level was perceived as the most challenging regarding gameplay flow and puzzle integration (Q5, Q6) due to its longer action sequence, more NPC interactions, branching paths, and layered puzzles, in contrast to the more linear Chile and China levels. A unified word cloud analysis (Q7) identified "Educational," "Cultural," "Immersive," and "Thoughtful" as the most frequent descriptors (Fig. 8), affirming the game's strong potential to bridge entertainment and health education effectively.

**LIMITATIONS:**
The preliminary validation utilized simulated user feedback generated by ChatGPT 4o based on predefined "mega-personas," which may not fully capture the nuances and diversity of real-world human user experiences and perceptions.

**KEY CONCEPTS:**
Serious Game, Bone Cancer Awareness, Point-and-Click Adventure, Simulated User Feedback, Mega-Personas, ChatGPT 4o, Chondrosarcoma, Ewing’s Sarcoma, Osteosarcoma, Game-Based Learning.
